question: Why is the deity called Pati and identified as wholly auspicious Shiva?
premises: Teachers explain the deity through etymologies in the scripture on the body of Shiva.
He commands, restrains, protects, and matures, thereby benefiting all.
Because of these functions he is called Pati, and in him there is nothing inauspicious.
inference: The lordship of Shiva is defined by beneficent governance, so his nature is entirely auspicious.
uncertainties: The compound śāsanarodhanapālanapācanayoga compresses several functions traditionally associated with the term Pati.
plain_english: Thus, by etymological explanations in the scripture on the body of Shiva, the teachers have taught the god: because he commands, restrains, protects, and matures, he benefits all. Therefore he is Pati, and Shiva is indeed wholly auspicious; there is nothing inauspicious in him.
